topic: Hazard-lift identification of staggered-adoption ATT in aliased hidden Markov panels. Fix a known finite hidden order K, finite untreated-output alphabet, T>=2K-1, time-homogeneous untreated HMM law, adoption hazard depending on current hidden state but conditionally independent of future untreated innovations, full predictive Hankel rank, invertible killed dynamics, and positive cohort masses. Prove that hazards in the current-emission algebra identify every adopter cohort's finite untreated counterfactual output law and group-time ATT despite non-permutation latent fibers. Prove a generic converse when aliased states have unequal hazards and unequal forecasts, including an exact positive same-observed-law fiber with ATT gap 2/185. On a predeclared fixed Hankel chart and coefficient-normalized polynomial frame with positive rank/frame gaps, derive joint influence functions and simultaneous fixed-grid inference; put algebra-collision sequences in an explicit gray zone. Consumer: Kim--Lee's six-period binary video-on-demand staggered-adoption panel. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact symbolic checks verified the canonical stopped-law realization, HDK invariance, two strictly positive three-state fibers, stochastic and similarity identities, invariant positive-fiber means, the 2/185 negative-fiber gap, full length-two ranks, and an 8/285 converse derivative. Differentiating the fixed Gram solve, de-killing inverse, matrix powers, and quotient yielded the panel-level influence expansion. The aliased witness frame has singular values 2.00332688 and 0.99833932; along a legal rank-three collision sequence, the declared chart has sigma3=(10.33271+o(1))*delta, so fixed separation keeps the exact repeated-emission witness while excluding false uniform root-N claims. Bounded primary checks found HMM alias geometry and outcome-driven adoption simulations, but no causal hazard-lift ATT theorem. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Apply the predeclared K=3 chart, HDK residual, frame-gap, cohort-mass, and influence-precision diagnostics to the six-period Kim--Lee panel and establish that at least one preregistered observable stratum is empirically usable. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the stated Hankel singular value, legal fibers, 2/185 gap, and analytic derivative, then run the fixed diagnostics on Kim--Lee; kill the application claim if every chart is ill-conditioned, HDK fails, precision is unusable, or the law lies in the collision gray zone. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_hazard_hmm_att.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Under known finite hidden order, full predictive Hankel rank, invertible killed dynamics, positive cohort masses, and adoption hazards in the current-emission algebra, does the observed stopped panel law identify every adopter cohort's finite untreated output law and group-time ATT across all non-permutation aliased HMM realizations, with failure generically witnessed when aliased states have unequal hazards and forecasts?

source_refs.claim: Kim and Lee estimate group-time effects in a six-period Netflix-IPTV panel under observed-history adjustment and report that lagged outcomes predict subsequent adoption.
source_refs.author: Suehyun Kim and Kwonsang Lee

source_refs.claim: Aliased HMM states share output distributions, and the paper characterizes non-permutation equivalence for the special case of two aliased states without studying causal cohort forecasts.
source_refs.author: Roi Weiss and Boaz Nadler

source_refs.claim: A latent-Markov event-history model permits a stopping event to depend on the shared hidden state, but does not identify untreated potential-outcome laws or ATT.
source_refs.author: Francesco Bartolucci and Alessio Farcomeni

source_refs.claim: Group-time ATT is identified under conditional parallel trends given observed covariates, not through a latent state-dependent adoption mechanism recovered from the outcome process.
source_refs.author: Brantly Callaway and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna

source_refs.claim: Generic finite-window HMM identifiability leaves exceptional aliased parameter varieties outside its guarantee and does not characterize causal functionals on their fibers.
source_refs.author: Elizabeth S. Allman, Catherine Matias, and John A. Rhodes

open_problems.why_unsolved: Staggered-DiD methods condition on observed histories, while latent-Markov event-history models use a shared hidden state without converting the stopped law into a causal identifying device. Existing HMM theorems either impose distinct emissions or study latent-parameter equivalence rather than invariance of a cohort counterfactual functional. The missing proof must show that hazard-marked killed observable operators determine cohort forecasts on the entire non-permutation realization fiber; conversely, it must identify the fiber direction that preserves all observed stopped words while moving ATT when hazards and future forecasts differ.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An observable-operator identification formula for every finite law P(Y_t(∞),...,Y_T(∞) | G=g) and ATT(g,t), an invariance theorem over admissible aliased realizations, and an exact strictly positive rational same-observed-law fiber with a certified nonzero ATT gap such as 2/185 outside the hazard-algebra condition.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination estimands, outcome-driven-adoption motivation, cohort structure, and six-period binary application.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Netflix adoption is staggered and prior viewing predicts adoption -> observed-history adjustment targets cohort-time effects -> latent behavioral states may jointly drive adoption and untreated viewing -> use the adoption hazard as an identifying measurement for cohort counterfactual laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Parameterize observationally equivalent aliased transition systems and determine which functions remain invariant over the resulting non-permutation fiber.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired counterfactual functional must be constant on exactly this kind of aliased HMM fiber.

method_exemplars.technique: Augment a latent Markov outcome model with a hidden-state-driven discrete event history and propagate the combined system through killed forward recursions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An adoption time is a state-dependent absorbing mark, although the destination must replace likelihood interpretation with an observable causal functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Stack cohort-time influence representations and use multiplier resampling for simultaneous inference over a fixed group-time grid.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once hazard lifting identifies untreated cohort means, the terminal object is the same finite vector of group-time ATT.

open_problems.open_problem: On a predeclared separated Hankel chart, can the empirical stopped-law-to-hazard-lift map be differentiated into joint influence functions and valid simultaneous fixed-grid ATT bands while explicitly excluding algebraic rank and coefficient-frame collision sequences from uniform root-n claims?

source_refs.author: Daniel Hsu, Sham M. Kakade, and Tong Zhang

source_refs.claim: Near-redundant HMMs can invalidate numerical curvature diagnostics and produce severely misleading conventional confidence intervals.

source_refs.claim: Multiplier-bootstrap procedures provide simultaneous inference for finite collections of regularly identified group-time ATT.
source_refs.author: Brantly Callaway and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna

open_problems.why_unsolved: Spectral-learning results control prediction error under singular-value separation, and staggered-DiD results supply simultaneous inference after regular influence functions are available. Neither literature differentiates the composed causal map formed by a selected Hankel chart, coefficient Gram solve, killed-dynamics inversion, matrix powers, and cohort quotient. Its derivative can diverge near rank or frame collisions, so pointwise delta-method calculations do not establish uniform root-n validity or specify an honest gray zone.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit stacked influence function and consistent covariance estimator for the finite ATT grid, a valid multiplier or Gaussian simultaneous band under declared rank, frame, inverse, and cohort-mass gaps, and a legal collision sequence proving failure of uniform root-n inference when those gaps vanish.

writing_exemplar.why: It makes simultaneous uncertainty for the six-period cohort-time effect grid the directly relevant empirical deliverable.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The application targets many correlated cohort-time effects -> conclusions require joint uncertainty -> hazard-lift estimates are smooth only on separated realization charts -> provide simultaneous regular inference and disclose the collision gray zone.

method_exemplars.technique: Express observable-operator recovery as GMM, differentiate the moment solution, and propagate moment covariance through its Jacobian.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed estimator is likewise a differentiable finite-moment solve before de-killing and ATT composition.

method_exemplars.technique: Stack group-time influence functions and calibrate a multiplier bootstrap to their fixed-grid maximum.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The final output is the same finite cohort-time ATT vector, so its simultaneous-band argument supplies the closest terminal proof step.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze drifting sequences indexed by identification strength and locate where ordinary expansions and confidence procedures cease to be uniform.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Shrinking Hankel and coefficient-frame singular values provide the natural identification-strength sequences for the hazard-lift chart.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Observed-history balance does not establish that a short binary panel supports a rank-three predictive realization, that adoption hazards lie in the required observable algebra, or that de-killing is numerically stable. Existing HMM diagnostics assess parameter redundancy or likelihood curvature separately rather than providing a simultaneous certificate for causal use. Searching across charts or strata after seeing their conditioning would invalidate nominal guarantees, so chart choice and multiplicity control must be fixed before inspecting the application.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A level-controlled joint diagnostic with predeclared chart and stratum rules, explicit critical values and separated-alternative power, followed by an empirical result that either confidence-certifies a usable K=3 stratum or formally classifies every stratum as rejected, imprecise, or collision-adjacent.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact data dimensions, cohort-time estimands, binary outcome, and Netflix-IPTV question the diagnostics must serve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The panel has substantively useful adoption cohorts but only six periods -> latent-state identification may be possible yet fragile -> observable rank, algebra, support, and precision restrictions must be checked before causal use -> certify a usable stratum or transparently kill the application.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate exhaustive observable summaries to distinguish estimable combinations from redundant latent-parameter directions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The certificate must detect exact and near nonidentification without trusting an unstable latent-likelihood Hessian.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate concentration of empirical word-probability matrices into singular-subspace and observable-operator error bounds under a smallest-singular-value gap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the direct proof route for uncertainty-aware Hankel-rank and chart-conditioning diagnostics in a finite panel.

method_exemplars.technique: Use multiplier resampling to control simultaneous error over a predeclared finite collection of cohort-time statistics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The diagnostic coordinates and final ATT estimates form fixed finite grids whose joint sampling uncertainty must be controlled.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature shows that endogenous dynamic treatment can lead to partial rather than point identification, while the closest prior CausalSmith construction explicitly leaves approximate common transitions unresolved. Exact hazard algebra and homogeneous killed dynamics yield polynomial recovery equalities; after relaxation there is no unique counterfactual law. The required first step changes to optimizing ATT over a compact stochastic aliased-HMM fiber subject to observable residual inequalities, and changing active constraints makes ordinary delta-method inference neither sharp nor uniformly valid.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp finite-dimensional polynomial or semialgebraic characterization of every ATT endpoint as a function of epsilon, constructive attainment by compatible positive HMM-hazard systems, and an honest confidence procedure for the endpoint vector and sign-breakdown radius.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest motivation arc from a brittle exact panel restriction to an interpretable violation radius and breakdown analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact identifying restrictions deliver point estimates -> small violations can alter causal conclusions -> bound violations by an interpretable radius -> report sharp effect regions and the radius at which conclusions change.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode finite latent-state compatibility, stochasticity, and causal targets as polynomial constraints and globally optimize the target to obtain sharp bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The relaxed hazard-lift model is a finite discrete latent-variable fiber with polynomial equalities, inequalities, and a rational ATT objective.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive sharp potential-outcome distribution bounds from dynamic-panel restrictions and prove endpoint attainability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination is likewise a cohort counterfactual distribution under endogenous dynamic selection, with finite-HMM restrictions sharpening the feasible set.

method_exemplars.technique: Bootstrap-calibrate relaxed sample moment restrictions and project the resulting feasible set onto a target while retaining uniform coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The ATT endpoints are projections of a nonlinear equality-and-inequality-constrained HMM parameter set whose active constraints can change.

open_problems.open_problem: For a fixed known K and separated hazard-lift chart, what is the semiparametric efficient influence function for the joint vector of cohort untreated path laws and group-time ATT under the complete time-homogeneous killed-HMM restrictions?

source_refs.excerpt: The unresolved content is constrained-model efficiency.
parameterize the constrained tangent space on the finite support and state a concrete normal-equations estimator

open_problems.why_unsolved: Differentiating the saturated multinomial stopped-law recovery map produces a valid influence function but does not exploit common untreated kernels, latent Markov factorization, or cross-period overidentification. The missing step is to parameterize the observed score space of a killed HMM modulo similarity and non-permutation alias fibers, then project the chart derivative onto this quotient tangent space. Without that projection, neither the canonical gradient nor any efficiency gain over the saturated plug-in is established.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A quotient-tangent-space theorem giving the canonical gradient and information bound for the full cohort-law and ATT vector, an estimator attaining that bound, and a criterion for strict variance improvement over the empirical stopped-law plug-in.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides a concrete finite cohort-time effect vector for which efficiency improvements have an immediate applied interpretation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Short panels contain many correlated cohort-time cells -> hazard lifting identifies their counterfactual laws -> the common latent dynamics impose additional cross-cell restrictions -> exploit those restrictions to attain the information bound.

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize efficient scores for conditional moment restrictions through generalized-inverse projection and construct an attaining minimum-distance estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Hazard-lift observable equations form a finite constrained moment model whose redundant latent directions must be quotiented before projecting the ATT derivative.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate a spectral latent-variable estimator and propagate empirical-moment fluctuations through recovered component functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest limit-theory template for a smooth chart-based latent reconstruction, although the destination must remain invariant to aliased realization fibers.

method_exemplars.technique: Describe the tangent directions generated by observational equivalence among aliased HMM realizations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those directions must be removed from the causal model's score space before its efficient ATT gradient is defined.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fixed positive rank and frame gaps make the Gram solve, de-killing inverse, matrix powers, and ATT quotient differentiable but do not locate the boundary at which their exploding derivatives can still be regularized without changing the target. The prior spectral-panel proposal leaves the selected-rank pseudoinverse frontier open. Here the first proof step must propagate stabilization bias through the entire stopped-law composition and then construct contiguous positive killed-HMM alternatives in the target-active collision direction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A phase theorem indexed by the smallest Hankel and coefficient-frame gaps, with an observable stabilization rule and honest fixed-grid band on the attainable sequences and a matching two-path lower bound on the complementary sequences.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames weak latent rank as an inferential boundary rather than merely a numerical problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent low-rank structure makes otherwise inaccessible targets estimable -> weak directions destabilize ordinary spectral recovery -> regularized projections preserve inference on part of the weak regime -> hazard-lift ATT requires its own Hankel-gap phase boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct inference for low-rank linear functionals without consistently estimating rank and prove validity across weak-factor sequences.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination also targets a low-rank causal functional under unstable empirical rank, but adds nonlinear de-killing and cohort normalization.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate the Moore-Penrose inverse on constant-rank strata and isolate derivative terms that diverge near rank change.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the first terms in the hazard-lift influence map that become singular when a declared Hankel chart approaches collision.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct drifting weak-identification experiments and establish validity or impossibility across identification-strength regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Shrinking rank and frame gaps index the local alternatives needed for a sharp uniform-inference frontier.

literature_map:
Kim and Lee (2025, arXiv:2511.23208) formulate cohort-time effects in a six-period Netflix-IPTV panel and adjust for observed histories while documenting outcome-predictive adoption.
Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021, Journal of Econometrics) provide the canonical group-time ATT framework, doubly robust estimation, and simultaneous bootstrap inference under conditional parallel trends.
Sun and Abraham (2021, Journal of Econometrics, DOI:10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.09.006) show contamination of conventional event-study coefficients under heterogeneous staggered effects.
Imai, Kim, and Wang (2023, AJPS, DOI:10.1111/ajps.12685) match panel observations on treatment and covariate histories but do not identify adoption through latent outcome states.
Abbring and van den Berg (2003, Econometrica, DOI:10.1111/1468-0262.00456) demonstrate that treatment timing can identify causal duration models under structural hazard restrictions.
Bartolucci and Farcomeni (2015, Biometrics, DOI:10.1111/biom.12224) couple latent Markov outcomes to an informative event-history process, the closest noncausal analogue of state-dependent adoption marking.
Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/09-AOS689) establish generic finite-window HMM identification but leave exceptional alias varieties outside the guarantee.
Gassiat, Cleynen, and Robin (2016, Statistics and Computing, DOI:10.1007/s11222-014-9523-8) identify finite-state HMMs under linearly independent emissions, excluding aliasing.
Alexandrovich, Holzmann, and Leister (2016, Biometrika, DOI:10.1093/biomet/asw001) weaken emission independence to distinctness but still exclude exactly equal emissions.
Weiss and Nadler (2015, ICML, arXiv:1502.02158) characterize HMMs with two aliased states but do not study causal treatment timing or cohort counterfactuals.
Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang (2012, JCSS, arXiv:0811.4413) recover observable HMM operators spectrally, with finite-sample behavior governed by smallest singular values.
Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez (2016, AISTATS, arXiv:1603.08815) cast spectral HMM learning as GMM, supplying a regular moment-estimation route to influence functions.
Cole (2019, METRON, DOI:10.1007/s40300-019-00156-3) studies HMM redundancy and warns that conventional numerical curvature diagnostics can fail near singularity.
Jun, Lee, and Shin (2016, JBES, DOI:I:10.1080/07350015.2015.1044008) derive dynamic-panel counterfactual bounds under endogenous treatment, but do not exploit finite-HMM stopped-law restrictions.
The scan found no paper combining aliased-HMM observable fibers, state-dependent adoption hazards, staggered cohort counterfactual laws, and simultaneous ATT inference.
